pr.title: Play a SuperCollider instrument from field keys through a voice host (keyboard-instrument.md chunk 2)
pr.head: b35267b94290ad445351aa5283c1df3ab426b9b4

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a virtual MIDI source named Field Keys; chunk 1, in #178, built that. This pull request lets it also play a SuperCollider instrument live. Inside a project, field keys still-water-pad plays shared/instruments/still-water-pad.scd from the keyboard and from every other MIDI source, so you can hear how a sound responds under your fingers instead of only rendering it offline.

Field's instruments are sclang programs that render one WAV from a spec passed in environment variables. An instrument becomes playable by answering a second mode: when FIELD_MODE is voice, the program's value is a SynthDef with freq, amp, gate, and out controls. A voice host, which is sclang running Field's sc/voice-host.scd, boots its own scsynth on the output device, adds that SynthDef, and starts one voice per note.

Two findings from running it shaped the edges. On macOS scsynth opens the default input device even with no input channels, and that waits on the microphone permission, so the host names one device, the output, for both directions, and field-audiod --keys now reports the system output's name. And scsynth keeps computing at the rate it booted at when the device's rate changes, which leaves every voice out of tune, so the host restarts its server when the measured rate drifts more than 1% from the booted one.

The first review, of 1e9e8d6, found four ways the voice host could hang or misbehave, and four commits fix them. The host now watches its own boot rather than trusting waitForBoot, quitting no longer waits for the host to be ready, a server that has not bound its port yet is stopped by its process, and the device name is checked before any server starts. The review of b35267b found the head clean, with two suggestions.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• sclang and scsynth. SuperCollider's language interpreter and its audio server. sclang runs programs and sends the server OSC messages over UDP.
  • Render mode. The existing contract: the program reads FIELD_SEED, FIELD_OUTPUT, and the rest, renders offline, and exits.
  • Voice mode. FIELD_MODE=voice: the program renders nothing, and its value is a SynthDef that plays one note.
  • Voice host. sclang on sc/voice-host.scd. It owns everything between MIDI and voices.
  • @field lines. The only lines Field reads from the host's stdout: @field followed by one JSON object (ready, restarting, error, and traced voices).
  • Rate restart. Quitting and rebooting scsynth at the device's new rate when it moves.

cards.title: Review and what is still owed
cards.html:

groups.title: The voice contract, answered by still-water-pad
groups.kicker: What an instrument returns to be playable, and the one instrument that does
intro: The render contract does not change. An instrument opts in to live play by checking FIELD_MODE first: in voice mode it must not render or exit, and its last expression must be a SynthDef whose gate control releases an envelope that ends in doneAction: 2, so the voice frees itself. The host sets freq from the note, amp from the velocity divided by 127, and out to bus 0.

still-water-pad is the first instrument to answer. Its voice is a gated version of the twelve-sine pad: three slightly detuned voices panned across the field, under an Env.asr. Its render branch is the old program re-indented inside the else function.

files.note: Wraps the existing render program in an if on FIELD_MODE and returns a gated SynthDef in voice mode.

checks.text: The author compared renders for seed 90210 before and after the edit with cmp and found them identical (criterion 27). This review did not rerun it. The file's content hash still changes, so every song that places the pad renders it once more.

groups.title: The voice host turns MIDI into voices
groups.kicker: sc/voice-host.scd: loading the voice, booting the server, playing notes, and cleaning up
intro: The host reads its inputs from the environment: the instrument's path, the UDP port Field chose for scsynth, the parent's process id, and an optional device. It runs the instrument with executeFile inside try. A load error, a value that is not a SynthDef, or a device it cannot use prints an @field error and exits 1. Everything after those checks lives in one function, run, because sclang's exit does not stop the code that called it.

run sets the server options: no input channels, two outputs, a 128-frame hardware buffer, no sample rate, and the device for both directions. Then it connects every MIDI source, registers handlers for note-on, note-off, sustain (CC 64), All Notes Off (CC 123), and pitch bend, and starts two routines. One compares the booted and measured rates every 0.7 seconds and restarts the server past 1%. The other checks once a second that field keys is alive, and stops the server and exits when it is not.

The host boots the server itself and watches it every 0.1 seconds, because SuperCollider's waitForBoot never calls its onFailure. It reports the server's process on a server_pid line as soon as one exists, prints ready once the server answers, and fails, naming the device, when the server's process exits first or 20 seconds pass. Until the server answers, a flag named booting makes note-ons do nothing.

files.note: The whole voice host: environment, load and device checks, server options, MIDI handlers, the boot watcher, the rate and parent checks, and the @field lines.

checks.text: scsynth falls back to the default input and output for a name it cannot find, which opens the microphone, and SuperCollider pastes the name between bare double quotes into the /bin/sh -c command that boots scsynth. So the host refuses a name ServerOptions.outDevices does not list, and one with ", a backtick, $, or \.

A suggestion from the review: on a rate restart, boot runs on /done /quit, which scsynth sends before it cleans up and exits, so server.pid can still hold the old process at this first check. If the old server outlives the first 0.1-second tick, launched captures it, and the restart either fails as exited or reports the old process. Accepting only a pid different from the one boot started with closes that. The review could not measure the exit time without running scsynth.
A restart clears the voice table without releasing voices, because quitting the server ends them, and sets booting so note-ons wait for the new server.
Bend moves every sounding voice on every channel by up to two semitones, and a new note starts at the current bend.
The parent check stops the server by its process, not by /quit, so a server still booting stops too.

groups.title: One place finds sclang
groups.kicker: sclangCommand() serves renders and the voice host alike
intro: runScProgram used to run FIELD_SCLANG or sclang and retry the SuperCollider.app bundle after an ENOENT. A long-running spawn cannot retry that way, so the lookup now happens before the spawn. sclangCommand() resolves FIELD_SCLANG, as a path or a name on PATH, then sclang on PATH, then the app bundle. A missing override still throws rather than falling back, because FIELD_SCLANG is the escape hatch for a deterministic wrapper.

files.note: Adds onPath and sclangCommand(), and has runScProgram call it. programPath now takes just the source.

checks.text: The stub-only runScProgram edges tests in src/graph/build.test.ts (missing override, timeout, stdout in failures) pass at this head, so the error messages are unchanged.

groups.title: The helper names the system output
groups.kicker: field-audiod --keys adds output to its ready line on macOS
intro: The host must name a device for both directions, so without --device it needs the system output's name, and only native code reads it. The helper that publishes Field Keys already runs JUCE, so it scans JUCE's CoreAudio device type and puts the default output's name on its ready line. Elsewhere the field is absent, and scsynth keeps its own defaults.

files.note: Adds defaultOutputDevice() and the ready line's output field.

checks.text: Built field-audiod at this head on macOS. The native round trip, which now requires output on macOS, passes against it.

files.note: Accepts the optional output field and keeps it as defaultOutput.

checks.text: On macOS this now requires output, and the native round trip passes against field-audiod built at this head.

groups.title: Starting, watching, and stopping the host from TypeScript
groups.kicker: VoiceHost in src/keys/voice-host.ts, tested against a stub sclang
intro: VoiceHost.start binds and releases a UDP port to choose one for scsynth, spawns sclang -D on the host script with the environment above, and resolves at once, so a host can be closed while it boots. Its ready promise settles on the first ready line. When sclang exits first, ready rejects with the host's error plus what sclang printed after its startup banner, which leaves out the class library's compile log.

close() sends an OSC /quit straight to the chosen port, gives the server process the host reported 500 ms to exit, and sends it SIGTERM if it is still running, because a server still booting has not bound its port and never sees /quit. Then it stops sclang with SIGTERM, and SIGKILL after three seconds.

files.note: Resolves the instrument path, picks the port, spawns and parses the host, and quits it.

checks.text: stopServer runs from close() and again whenever sclang exits, so a server outlives neither a quit nor a host that dies on its own.
All 13 tests pass at this head, and no stub server outlived the run.
The stub here launches a sleep that ignores /quit and reports it as server_pid, so the test passes only if close() stops it by process.

groups.title: The field keys <instrument> command
groups.kicker: The command resolves the instrument, starts the host after the helper, and shows its state
intro: field keys takes an optional instrument and a --device option. It resolves the instrument before the terminal goes raw: a bare name gains .scd and resolves on the project's shared/instruments/ shelf, as a supercollider: entry's source: does, and a path resolves from the project root, or from the current directory outside a project.

It starts the host after the helper, so Field Keys exists when sclang connects its MIDI inputs, and the keyboard plays while the host boots. A rejected ready stops field keys with the reason. The status line gains the instrument's state: starting, live at a rate on a device, or restarting. On quit it sends note-offs and All Notes Off, closes the host whether or not it is ready, and closes the helper.

files.note: Adds resolveInstrument, starts and closes the host, and adds the instrument to the status line.

checks.text: A path with a slash resolves from the project root, not the current directory, as docs/keys.md now says.
Without --device, the host gets the helper's system output name, which it checks against ServerOptions.outDevices before booting.
Quitting closes the host directly, so a host that never becomes ready cannot hold field keys open.

groups.title: Docs and the plan
groups.kicker: How to play an instrument and make one playable, and chunk 2 recorded as built
intro: docs/keys.md gains a section on playing an instrument and a reference for voice mode. docs/build-graph.md states voice mode beside the render contract, docs/architecture.md's live SuperCollider mode now describes the voice host, and the README mentions it. The plan corrects §2.6's No inputs bullet, noting what it replaced as the repository's plan conventions ask, adds the ready line's output field to §2.5, and appends §10, chunk 2 as built, whose §10.2 records the four fixes from review.

checks.text: Now says where a path resolves from: the project root inside a project, and the current directory outside one.
§10.1 showed this fix only on the speakers, which have no inputs.
A suggestion from the review: this row says 11 tests pass, and the file has 13 at this head, including the two close cases.

Criterion 21 uses the Apollo, which has inputs. For one named device scsynth starts a single IOProc with every stream on, inputs included, unless ServerOptions.inputStreamsEnabled turns them off. Watch for a microphone prompt there; the review could not confirm whether macOS shows one.
